text: We evaluated bootstrapping through an intermediate-size model, using gpt2-small as the weak supervisor, qwen2.5-1.5b as the intermediate model, and qwen2.5-3b as the strong student, across num_seeds = 3 seeds. The weak supervisor reaches 0.6 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling (trained on ground truth) is 0.82, while the bootstrapped transfer accuracy is 0.63 with a standard error of 0.03. The resulting performance gap recovered (PGR) is 0.14 with a standard error of 0.14, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.24 for direct weak-to-strong training. The measured PGR is therefore below the baseline and its standard error is as large as the point estimate itself, so these data provide no evidence that the intermediate-model bootstrapping pipeline recovers more of the gap than the baseline; with only three seeds the estimate is too imprecise to rank the two methods in either direction. Further seeds would be needed before drawing any directional conclusion.
